Avoid this clinic! The doctor is not competent, and rude and they only try to inflate the bill. Last month I went to the Ning clinic for an asthma attack and the doctor did not understand my condition at all. He gave me a 5 minute aerosol, rinsed my nose with saline solution telling me that I am lactose intolerant due to white spots near my nose (which is not true) and prescribed drugs for the absurd sum of 5000 baht. When I left there I was worse than before.
Furthermore the hygienic conditions of the place are terrible!!!!

A small clinic with a qualified doctor.
On vacation, my ear ached and we could not quickly find an insurance clinic, this clinic was next to us.
For 2500 baht, we were issued a document for insurance, examined, given 3 types of drop drugs and pills. The ear passed, as promised, in 4 days.
The next day we went to a clinic in Bangkok for insurance, this appointment cost the insurance too 2500 baht, but it was just an examination. So all prices are relative, and here you will help good people.

I recently visited Ning Clinic with severe pain in my left ear, and the experience was nothing short of alarming. The facility itself looked disturbingly unsanitary, as though cleanliness were more rumor than reality. The medical equipment appeared outdated and unclean, and it hardly inspired confidence in their sterilization methods.

To make matters worse, my encounter with Dr. Suphot Thaweethawonsawat was profoundly disappointing. He dismissed my thoughts about how the infection may have started, speaking to me as if I were an inconvenience rather than a patient. During the exam, he hastily placed a cotton wad in my ear without cleaning or sterilizing the area, causing additional pain and raising serious concerns about basic medical protocols.

When I asked about paying only for the consultation—since I already had antibiotics and preferred not to purchase more—he threatened to involve the police if I didn’t comply with his instructions. He even suggested removing the cotton (the one he’d just inserted) at an extra 1000bhat charge if I refused his medication. It's ridiculous... Needless to say, I left the clinic in worse pain than when I arrived, both physically and emotionally.

If you value professionalism, hygiene, and your peace of mind, I strongly recommend avoiding Ning Clinic at all costs. My visit has left me worried about the state of my ear and utterly shocked by how a supposed medical institution could operate this way. Very very bad.

It immediately brought me incredible relief, the pressure in my ear dropped, I felt better, now I'm still struggling with a low squealing sound in my ear which was in the process of diganosis but has dropped to 70%. If someone is bothered by the price of a visit, like most people write that the price is crazy, they could have read the price list left at the reception before entering the office. And so Thais pay the same as Farangs because I was a witness, so this nonsense is made up by people who think that they are entitled to everything for free.

text:
I couldn't equalize after landing and could barely hear the entire day of my arrival.
I then called the clinic at 4:55 p.m. and immediately got an appointment for the next morning at 9:30 a.m.

The clinic looks a bit unusual by European standards, but everyone was wearing masks and gloves, and the doctor disinfected all instruments during treatment. So I have no concerns about hygiene.

The young receptionists are very friendly and speak good English.
After they briefly took my medical history and measured my blood pressure, I was immediately allowed to sit down in the examination room.

The doctor came right after and asked me about my problems. I told him my ear was blocked and I would like to have my ear canals cleaned.
He did that and then examined my ears and nose with an electronic otoscope.
His diagnosis: incipient middle ear infection.

He then gave me helpful tips for everyday life, how to prevent it, performed a nasal irrigation, and administered medication.

I got all of that (shower, 2 sprays, drops, antibiotics, effervescent tablets) along with silicone earplugs for swimming.

Those helpful and pleasant 20 minutes cost me 3,300 baht.
I can't understand all the complainers here. The travel insurance covers the costs anyway. If you don't have any, you've probably taken the risk knowingly...
Especially since 3,300 baht for competent medical treatment + medication is affordable from a "Western perspective."

The "practice" doesn't look very trustworthy, either from the outside or the inside. Nevertheless, my ear infection was treated excellently there. Although I did suspect I should have been going more often than necessary. No matter, my international health insurance covered the bill without any problems.
He is a kind and competent doctor.
